unit.why: An anecdote about R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi visiting Probisht on his return from Petersburg, meeting Hava, wife of R. Shalom, and her sons, and the young Israel of Ruzhin asking him a question about the Shema.

stories.start_quote: העיד הרב החסיד איש האמת מו"ה יצחה
stories.end_quote: מפיו של הקדוש רש״ז מלאדי זצוק"ל
stories.summary_en: On his way back from Petersburg, R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi passed through Probisht, where the tsaddeket Hava brought her two sons to him; the seven- or eight-year-old Israel of Ruzhin asked how one can say ve-ahavta, which implies a sense of self, right after the first verse of the Shema, which requires self-sacrifice and the annulment of self; R. Shneur Zalman gave him a vast answer, and the child understood all of it.
